<reason>A made the stronger comparative case. B established genuine reach and access benefits, but repeatedly treated better recruitment as indispensable recruitment and subscription funding as merely short-term. A candidly answered the symmetrical-burden challenge, distinguished fragmentation from price exclusion, and explained why both choices carry long-term opportunity costs. A also directly rebutted B’s closing reversibility argument. Neither side quantified the tradeoff, but A handled the uncertainty and opposing pressure substantially better.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A used B’s own barbecue and relatives’ television examples to show that household subscriptions and free ordinary-season games still permit accidental discovery. This directly undermined B’s central leap from free marquee broadcasts enlarging recruitment opportunities to their absence deleting those opportunities.</best_rebuttal>
